title: fix(service-analytics)!: an analytics read gate that could not decide answers 503 SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE, not the denial's 403
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-sales"} -->
_Requested by **Sales** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01D5bWFY3rFzgJcytD5gD4Uu?thread=cmsg_01D5bWFY3rFzgJcytD5gD4UuDWJsBGQpadCH8JR2xZQ5re)_

Fixes #25561

Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none

## What was wrong

Three analytics door refusals are operator-side faults: a resolver threw or could not answer. All three answered with the same wire body as a real denial, `403 PERMISSION_DENIED` naming the object. A caller could not tell "you may not read this" from "the server could not decide".

| site | what happened | before | now |
|---|---|---|---|
| `read-admission.ts` `assertObjectsReadable`, catch branch | the object-level admission provider threw | 403 `PERMISSION_DENIED` (byte-identical to the `!admitted` branch) | 503 `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` |
| `field-read-admission.ts` (was `fieldReadUnresolvedError`) | the readable or queryable field reader threw | 403 `PERMISSION_DENIED` | 503 `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` |
| `api-exposure-door.ts` (was `exposureUnresolvedError`) | the object declaration lookup threw | 403 `PERMISSION_DENIED` | 503 `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` |

## What changed

- **One fault answer for the three gates.** `readAdmissionUnresolvedError` (in `read-admission.ts`, not exported from the package) throws `{ code: 'SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE', status: 503, object }`. `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` is an existing ADR-0112 `StandardErrorCode`, and it is the spelling `packages/core/src/security/authz-store-unavailable.ts` uses for the same class under the maintainer ruling quoted there. No code is added, and no envelope key is added. The two per-file fault constructors are removed and their call sites use the shared one.
- **No oracle.** The message names the object and nothing else: not which gate could not answer, not why, not whether the object exists. It says only that the server could not decide. The cause stays in the server log at each site, as before (`logger.error` with the cause).
- **Still fail-closed.** Every path that refused still refuses: the three catch branches still throw. Only the code and the status move.
- **Real denials are byte-unchanged.** The `!admitted` branch keeps `403 PERMISSION_DENIED`, and so do the field-level verdicts (`fieldReadDeniedError`, `fieldReadUnjudgeableError`). The exposure verdicts keep `404 OBJECT_API_DISABLED` / `405 OBJECT_API_METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED`.
- **The door.** `POST /api/v1/analytics/dataset/query` already relays a declared 5xx through the shared declared-fault arm (`declaredServerFaultAnswer`). So the fault reaches the caller as `503 {"code":"SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE","error":"Internal server error"}`, not `500 ANALYTICS_QUERY_FAILED`. The message is withheld, as for every declared server fault. The cube query door (`dispatcher-plugin` `errorResponseBase`) relays the declared status and code the same way. **No `packages/rest` source change.**
- **The consumer.** `packages/metadata-protocol/src/build-probes.ts` keyed its access fix on `PERMISSION_DENIED`. Without a change, a fault would have fallen to "Fix the dataset definition…", which is wrong for an outage. A `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` throw now gets its own fix: the dataset is not the cause; the server could not decide read access to the named object (falling back to the dataset's object); check the server log for the resolver that failed, then republish once it is healthy. The `code` (`widget_query_failed`), `severity` and `message` are unchanged.

## Tests

Measured on head `18b8b6fa5d (`service-analytics` and `metadata-protocol` files are byte-identical to their state at each run below; later commits touched only the rest test and the changeset)`:

- `@objectstack/service-analytics`, whole package: Test Files 185 passed (185), Tests 4517 passed | 262 skipped. Pins that asserted the 403 on a fault leg moved with the fix: `read-admission-gate.test.ts` (now across all three doors, both strategies; it also asserts the message names the object and not the cause), `field-read-admission-gate.test.ts` (reader throws, both strategies, plus the plugin bridge with no `getReadableFields`), `field-query-admission-gate.test.ts` (queryable reader throws, both strategies), `api-exposure-door.test.ts` (lookup throws; plugin with no data engine), `unexposed-definition-registration.test.ts` (query face after a throwing lookup). The real-denial twins in the same files stay `403 PERMISSION_DENIED` / `404` / `405`, untouched.
- `@objectstack/rest`, new `analytics-read-gate-fault-envelope.test.ts`: a seam test through the real route with a real `AnalyticsService`. For each of the three gates, a throwing resolver gives `503 SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` (not `PERMISSION_DENIED`, not `ANALYTICS_QUERY_FAILED`), the prose is withheld, nothing executes, the cause lands in the service log and the fault lands in the route log. The verdict twin of each gate answers `403 PERMISSION_DENIED`, `403 PERMISSION_DENIED` or `404 OBJECT_API_DISABLED`, and there is a positive control (200). The generic relay was already pinned for a hand-built declared 503; this file pins the producer and the route together. Test Files 1 passed, Tests 7 passed (re-run on 18b8b6fa5d); `src/analytics*` in `@objectstack/rest`: Test Files 23 passed (23), Tests 298 passed | 22 skipped.
- `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `build-probes-widget-refusal-fix.test.ts`: two new cases (`SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` with an object; without one, which falls back to the dataset's object). Whole package: Test Files 263 passed | 3 skipped (266), Tests 21472 passed | 19 skipped; the widget-refusal file 8/8 re-run on 18b8b6fa5d.
- `@objectstack/runtime` `http-dispatcher.test.ts` + `packages-publish-drafts-probe-caller-context.test.ts`: Test Files 2 passed, Tests 251 passed.
- Typecheck: `service-analytics`, `metadata-protocol` and `rest` all exit 0.

**Ablation (one site, predicted red).** With the fix committed, I reverted the read-admission catch branch to the denial (`throw readAdmissionDeniedError(...)`, tagged with a marker) through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`. Then I rebuilt `service-analytics`, and `ablation-dist-preflight` showed the marker present in `dist/index.js` and `dist/index.cjs`. Result: `read-admission-gate.test.ts` went **6 failed / 19 passed** (the fault case on all three doors × two strategies), and the rest seam went **1 failed / 6 passed** (the object-level fault row; the twins stayed green). Restore: blob equal to HEAD and `git diff HEAD` empty. After the rebuild, preflight `--absent` reported the marker absent from all 6 built files, the tree clean, and the rest seam back at 7/7.

## Gates

`node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` derived 72 commands. All 72 were run locally and reconciled with `--ran`: "72 derived, 72 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN (a DERIVED zero, all 72 recorded an exit code)". All exit 0 on 18b8b6fa5d. On the first pass `check-rest-log-spy-declared` was red on the new rest test (no `OS_REST_LOG` declared); that is fixed in this PR. Three gates were red only on tree state while a concurrent closure build was rewriting `dist/` (`check:dts-closure`, `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` PREREQUISITE, `check:type-check-debt` exit 3); each was re-run on the settled tree and exits 0. `pnpm lint` (repo-wide eslint): lock VERDICT command-exit 0. CI families are read from this PR's check-runs.

## Dogfood battery

18b8b6fa5d, `pnpm --filter @objectstack/dogfood test` after the `@objectstack/dogfood^...` closure build, under the verify lock: VERDICT command-exit 0. Test Files 291 passed | 3 skipped (294), Tests 2505 passed | 18 skipped (2523). No failures.

## Acceptance notes

- The object-level **plugin bridge** (`service-analytics/src/plugin.ts`, the `admitObjectRead` auto-bridge) answers `return false`, not a throw, in its UNUSABLE branch: a wired `security` service that cannot be resolved or exposes neither `canReadObject` nor `explain`. On the in-repo kernels that branch also covers a deployment that registers no security service. That is the same class (the server could not decide), but it arrives at `assertObjectsReadable` as a verdict, so it still answers `403 PERMISSION_DENIED`. It is outside this card's file surface and is left untouched here; see the report's out-of-scope findings. The field-level and exposure bridges throw, so they already answer 503 with this change (pinned: the bridge with no `getReadableFields`; the plugin with no data engine).
- On the wire the 503's message is withheld (`"Internal server error"`), as the declared-fault arm does for every declared 5xx. The fault is deliberately not marked `refusal: true`: it is a fault, not a refusal whose prose is authored for the caller. That matches the core precedent.
